provenance: Demo-scoped corrected subset. Structure follows the nyc.v2 draft (rules/proposals/); every fact carries an evidence reference to a fetch-confirmed primary-source quote in docs/VERIFICATION-SOURCES.md (Round 1 or Round 2, 2026-07-22) or an explicit RESEARCH_REQUIRED/OFFICIAL_CONFLICT status. No fact is asserted beyond fetched text. The full 59-rule draft remains in rules/proposals/ as the post-capstone target. CHANGE FROM nyc.v2.2: exactly one rule differs — DOB-ASSEMBLY-001's deadline gains "boundary": "exclusive". Its already-published qualification records the DOB code note that a TPA application 'must be submitted earlier than 10 days before the event', so day 10 is already too late and the last valid filing day is day 11. That was only stated in prose, which left the engine reading the bound as inclusive and reporting an event exactly 10 days out as at-risk rather than missed — under-claiming a closed window. The field makes the published bound machine-readable; absent, a deadline stays inclusive, which is what every other dated rule's wording ('at least', 'no later than') means. No new regulatory fact: the exclusivity was already published in the qualification text, and no source, verification status, trigger, calendar_days value, fee, agency or portal changed. CHANGE FROM nyc.v2.1 (carried forward in v2.2): DOHMH-ORGANIZER-NOTIFY-001 publishes output.disposition MAY_BE_REQUIRED, because Article 88 scope for free prepackaged distribution by the host is contested on file (VERIFICATION-SOURCES RF-4). Both changes move verdicts at a boundary, and a ruleset_version must identify fixed semantics for AD-7 replay and AD-13 version comparison to hold, so each was published under a new version rather than edited in place. snapshot_date is 2026-07-25, the date this version was published. F-206 defines it as published-on rather than verified-on, so it carries no claim that any fact was re-verified: no source was re-fetched, and the evidence in VERIFICATION-SOURCES.md remains the 2026-07-22 rounds. Holding it at 2026-07-22 would have understated the age of the exact version a plan banner names.

engine_conventions: Tri-state evaluation; material unknown propagates to CONDITIONAL, never silently false.

A rule's kind (permit, insurance, notification, registration, eligibility, prohibition, dependency, classification, advisory, note) describes what the rule is. A persisted finding's kind is usually the same, with one exception: a classification rule (SAPO-SCOPE-001) emits a note finding. Persisted finding kinds are therefore permit, insurance, notification, registration, eligibility, prohibition, dependency, advisory, note.

Findings carry a disposition (REQUIRED, MAY_BE_REQUIRED, PROHIBITED_OR_INELIGIBLE, ADVISORY, NO_NEW_REQUIREMENT_IDENTIFIED). A classification rule emits a note finding with the NO_NEW_REQUIREMENT_IDENTIFIED disposition, retaining its rule id for provenance. These rule-domain kind/disposition names are stored in the plan-item schema's lowercase form (note, no_new_requirement); see ARCHITECTURE.

Top-level verdict stays four-state (FEASIBLE / FEASIBLE-AT-RISK / CONDITIONAL / INFEASIBLE) computed from per-finding deadline statuses (ON_TRACK / DEADLINE_APPROACHING / PUBLISHED_DEADLINE_MISSED / NOT_CALCULABLE / NOT_APPLICABLE). INFEASIBLE copy reads 'published deadline missed as scoped' — a missed filing window, not a claim of legal impossibility.
RESEARCH_REQUIRED deadlines are listed, rendered 'confirm with agency', excluded from verdict arithmetic.
OFFICIAL_CONFLICT rules render both readings and their sources; they never resolve silently.
Empty permit set is first-class: 'no new city event requirement identified from the provided facts' plus triggered advisories.
